title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
The brands on your kitchen shelf are run by people doing extraordinary work that nobody sees.

We're building the platform they run on, and a brand they'll be proud to be part of.

Confido is the AI operating system that runs cash application, deductions, trade and planning in one place for CPG brands. That means Finance, Sales, and Ops finally work on the same number.

We’re trusted by 250+ brands managing $30B+ in revenue, including Daisy, OLIPOP, Simple Mills, Idahoan, and more. We've achieved best-in-class growth and recently raised a $55M Series B led by Insight Partners to accelerate our momentum.

If you want your work on shelves everywhere — and outsized ownership while you build — we'd love to meet you.

The Role

At Confido, data powers everything from customer-facing insights to internal decision making. We are looking for an Analytics / Data Engineer to build the foundation that enables scalable reporting, trusted metrics, and seamless data access across the company.

What You'll Do


Design, build, and maintain our centralized data warehouse and analytics infrastructure.
Develop scalable data models that power reporting, dashboards, operational workflows, and customer-facing data exports.
Serve as the steward of Confido's data landscape, creating visibility into data ownership, lineage, and dependencies while ensuring data is discoverable, trustworthy, and easy to consume across the organization.
Consolidate and standardize data models across multiple products and teams, creating a single source of truth for the business.
Establish data engineering best practices, including data modeling standards, testing, documentation, monitoring, and governance.
Partner closely with Engineering, Product, Operations, and Customer teams to define metrics and deliver actionable insights.
Improve data quality, reliability, and accessibility across the organization.
Enable self-service analytics by creating scalable datasets and semantic layers for downstream consumers.


What We're Looking For


4-8+ YOE building and operating modern data warehouses and analytics platforms.
Strong SQL skills and experience modeling large datasets.
Deep experience with distributed data processing, including designing performant ETL pipelines and optimizing large-scale data workloads.
Experience with data pipeline orchestration, ETL/ELT workflows, and data infrastructure.
Familiarity with modern analytics tooling such as Snowflake, dbt, or similar technologies.
Ability to balance immediate business needs with long-term platform investments.
Excellent communication skills and a track record of working cross-functionally with technical and non-technical stakeholders.


Success in This Role

Within your first year, you'll establish the foundation of Confido's analytics platform by building a scalable data warehouse, unifying fragmented data models across teams, and creating the infrastructure and standards that allow every engineer to reliably publish and consume data. Your work will directly enable faster decision-making, better customer insights, and a more data-driven organization.

title: Senior Analytics Engineer
description:
Senior Analytics Engineer for a Series B Venture backed Startup | New York City, NY | Hybrid Compensation: $180K–$211.5K base + equity




About the Company Our client is a fast-growing technology company building modern digital infrastructure for payments, transactions, and business operations.

As the company continues to scale its data and analytics capabilities, they are hiring a Senior Analytics Engineer to take foundational ownership of how core business metrics are defined, modeled, governed, and used across the organization. This is a highly visible role at the intersection of analytics engineering, data governance, business strategy, and cross-functional decision-making.




The Opportunity We are looking for a founding-level Senior Analytics Engineer to own the data stack from the gold layer onward. Our Data Engineering team handles raw ingestion, warehouse reliability, and the bronze-to-silver layers. This role picks up from there to ensure the organization has trusted, consistent, and reusable definitions for key business performance metrics. For example, operational performance and transaction throughput metrics should mean the same thing whether queried in a BI dashboard, surfaced through an internal Slack chatbot, or consumed by an LLM-based agent.




This is much more than a traditional transformation-pipeline role. The Senior Analytics Engineer will own semantic layers, metric definitions, data contracts, cross-team metric standardization, gold-layer modeling, certified data products, analytics cost management, and data context for both human and AI consumers.




What You'll Own

Own the gold layer and ensure core business metrics are modeled consistently and reliably.
Design and maintain the company’s semantic layer / metrics layer.
Define metrics and data contracts that are adopted across multiple teams.
Partner with stakeholders across the business to resolve disagreements around metric definitions.
Establish trusted, reusable data products that can support dashboards, reporting, self-service analytics, and AI/LLM-based consumers.
Partner on the company’s broader reporting and analytics revamp.
Expand data capture and improve the quality and usability of business-critical datasets.
Help manage and optimize analytics infrastructure costs, including Snowflake and dbt usage.
Improve documentation and create a more scalable, writing-first analytics culture.
Work closely with Data Engineering while maintaining clear ownership of analytics-layer modeling and governance.

What We're Looking For

5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data analytics, or a closely related field.
Strong, clearly demonstrated advanced SQL experience.
Strong experience with dbt and Snowflake.
Direct ownership of a semantic layer, metrics layer, or equivalent modeling framework.
Experience defining metrics or data contracts adopted by multiple teams.
Experience acting as the sole or lead analytics engineer for important modeling or metric work.
Track record of resolving cross-functional disagreements around how business metrics should be defined.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to operate independently in a decentralized, fast-moving environment.

Particularly Relevant Experience

dbt Semantic Layer, LookML / Looker, Cube, Sigma, self-service analytics tooling, semantic modeling, metrics governance, or data contracts.
Snowflake or dbt cost optimization.
Airbyte or Fivetran.
LLM or AI-enabled data products, structured chatbot context, MCP-style interfaces, or data products used by AI agents.
Client-facing analytics or consulting work.
A master’s degree in a relevant discipline is a plus, but not required.

Ideal Background

The strongest candidates may have worked as Senior Analytics Engineer, Lead Analytics Engineer, Staff Analytics Engineer, Founding Analytics Engineer, Analytics Engineering Manager interested in returning to an IC role, or Senior Data Analyst with significant analytics-engineering and modeling ownership.
Strong candidates often come from high-growth startups or high-caliber technology companies that use a modern data stack (e.g., payments platforms, business software, SaaS, or high-growth tech unicorns).

What Success Looks Like The ideal candidate is not simply someone who builds data models. They are someone who can step into a company where different teams may have different interpretations of the same metric and create a clear, trusted source of truth.

You should be comfortable asking questions such as: What does this metric actually mean? Who should own its definition? Why are two teams calculating it differently? Which version should become the company standard? How should that definition be represented in dbt, BI tools, and future AI applications?

The strongest person for this role combines technical depth, business curiosity, and strong cross-functional judgment.

Green Flags

Founding or first analytics-engineering ownership at a startup.
Direct ownership of semantic or metrics infrastructure.
Strong Snowflake + dbt experience.
Clear examples of creating metrics or data contracts used by multiple teams.
Experience resolving disagreements between Product, Finance, Operations, or other business teams around metric definitions.
Strong documentation habits and writing-first communication.
Initiative beyond the formal job description.
Experience thinking about how analytics models support both BI tools and AI agents.
Experience with AI, LLMs, or agentic data consumers.

What May Not Be a Fit

Data engineering infrastructure, orchestration, or ingestion with limited analytics modeling.
Pipeline development without meaningful SQL/dbt ownership.
Analytics roles without ownership of shared metrics or semantic layers.
Highly academic or research-heavy backgrounds with limited production experience.
Candidates who have mainly contributed to models owned by a centralized Data Engineering team rather than leading analytics-layer ownership themselves.

Location & Compensation

Location: New York City, NY — Hybrid.
Compensation: $180K–$210K base salary + equity.
Relocation and visa sponsorship may be considered on a case-by-case basis.

Why This Role Is Interesting This is an opportunity to become the person who defines how the company understands and uses its own data. Rather than inheriting a fully mature analytics function, you will have the chance to shape the company’s semantic layer, establish metric governance, influence how teams make decisions, and build data products that will eventually serve both people and AI systems.

title: Software / Data Engineer (First Technology Hire - NYC Private Equity)
description:
How would you like to be the first technology hire at a NYC private equity firm - handed a blank sheet of paper to build their entire tech stack and data strategy from the ground up?




What's The Job?

As our first technology hire, you will own the modernization of our tech stack and the build-out of our data strategy. Almost nothing is built yet. Outside of Microsoft 365 and our CRM, you are choosing the tools.




Day to day, you will be:

Building the data foundation our investment, asset management and finance teams run on - pipelines, integrations, and one source of truth for portfolio and property data.
Automating the manual processes that live in spreadsheets and inboxes today, using Python, SQL, Power Automate and Power Apps.
Standing up reporting and dashboards in Power BI so the partners can see performance without waiting on a manual roll-up.
Connecting our CRM, accounting systems and third-party real estate data sources.
Acting as the internal expert - recommending the platforms we adopt and owning the roadmap we follow.




We have an experienced outside technology advisor and consultancy we have utilized in the past you can liaise with, so you are not figuring this out alone. You will report directly to our CFO and have partner-level exposure from your first week.

We are a New York City private equity firm founded in 2014, investing in real estate and real estate platform companies. We have several billion in assets under management and expect to pass $5B shortly. We are a 25-person team based on Park Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, and we have never had a technology function. You would be building it.




What Skills Do You Need?

- 1-4 years of professional experience as a Software Engineer, Data Engineer, Analytics Engineer, Data Analyst, Business Intelligence Developer or Business Systems Analyst.

- Strong SQL, plus Python (or similar) for automation and data work.

- Working knowledge of the Microsoft ecosystem: Microsoft 365, Power BI, Power Automate / Power Apps. Azure, Microsoft Fabric or SQL Server are a plus.

- Experience building or maintaining data pipelines, ETL, system integrations or reporting.

- Real business curiosity. You will be sitting with the CFO and the partners, not behind a ticket queue.

- The polish and professional maturity to operate inside a private equity firm.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related field.

- You must be a US Citizen or Green Card Holder. We are not able to provide visa sponsorship now or in the future.




Compensation

$125,000 - $175,000 base salary
Annual bonus, targeted at 15-30% in year one
Full benefits package
4 days on site in our Park Avenue office (Monday-Thursday), remote on Fridays




What's In It For You?

This is the rare early-career role with genuine ownership. You are not the fortieth engineer maintaining somebody else's pipeline. You pick the stack, you set the roadmap, and you get the credit for it in front of the partners of the firm. This seat is built to grow - the person who executes here becomes our technology leader.

description:
Company Overview

Position Overview




THIS IS A HYBRID ROLE BASED IN MONTVALE, NJ




The Senior Power BI Developer owns the dashboards and reporting our business runs on. This is a Power BI–first, stakeholder-facing role: the majority of the work is designing, building, and maintaining Power BI dashboards — and partnering directly with Finance, Operations, Sales, and Marketing to turn ambiguous business questions into clear, trusted, decision-ready analytics.

You'll work on top of a curated BigQuery reporting layer maintained by our data engineering function, so you can focus on the semantic model, the metrics, the visuals, and the business conversation — not on building pipelines. A baseline understanding of data architecture (how a layered warehouse and dimensional models are structured) is important so you can collaborate effectively with data engineering and design performant, reliable reports. This role is ideal for someone who is a genuine Power BI craftsperson and equally comfortable sitting with a business leader to figure out what they actually need.




Essential Job Functions




Dashboard & Report Development (the core of the role)

Build and maintain Power BI dashboards — design, develop, and iterate interactive dashboards and reports on the curated reporting layer, using DAX, Power Query (M), and strong data-modeling and visualization practices.
Own the Power BI semantic model — build and maintain star-schema data models, relationships, measures, and calculation logic that are performant and reusable across reports.
Optimize performance — tune models, DAX, and queries for speed and reliability; make deliberate Import vs. DirectQuery choices and manage refresh/query cost against BigQuery.




Stakeholder Partnership & Business Intelligence

Understand the business problem — partner with Finance, Operations, Sales, and Marketing to translate ambiguous questions into well-defined KPIs, metric definitions, and the right visuals — confirming the requirement before building.
Tell the story — apply data-visualization best practices to turn data into clear, usable insight — not just charts, but answers a stakeholder can act on.
Enable self-service — promote trusted, well-documented reports and datasets, and help business users get value from them independently.
Document and build repeatable processes — maintain strong, clear documentation of requirements, metric definitions, and reporting logic, and establish repeatable processes and standards for how reporting requests are intake, prioritized, built, and validated.




Publishing, Governance & Report Lifecycle

Deploy and operate in the Power BI Service — publish and manage workspaces, apps, and scheduled/gateway-managed refreshes; own reports through their full lifecycle including maintenance, troubleshooting, and UAT.
Apply security and governance — implement row-level security (RLS) and follow governance best practices so the right people see the right data.
Document — maintain metric definitions, data-model documentation, and report catalogs so reporting is understandable and maintainable.




Collaboration with Data Engineering

Work the DE / BI seam — the data engineering function owns ingestion, pipelines, and the raw/transformed layers; you own the reporting layer and everything Power BI. Partner on data contracts, required datasets, freshness expectations, and reporting-layer schema so dashboards are built on a trusted foundation.

Core must-haves

Power BI mastery — hands-on expertise across DAX, Power Query (M), data modeling, and row-level security — able to build and maintain dashboards independently, end to end.
Advanced SQL — writing and optimizing complex queries (BigQuery preferred).
Stakeholder & requirements skill — proven ability to gather requirements, translate business questions into metrics, and communicate clearly with non-technical audiences.
Data-visualization judgment — a strong sense for visual best practices, dashboard UX, and data storytelling.
Baseline data architecture understanding — dimensional modeling (star/snowflake), layered warehouse concepts, and how curated datasets are produced — enough to collaborate with data engineering and design reliable reports.

Plus

5–7 years in business intelligence, Power BI development, analytics, or a related field.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Analytics, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.
Strong problem-solving, a business-first mindset, and excellent cross-functional communication.
Ability to connect Power BI directly to a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery preferred), not just flat files.

Certifications — Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate (PL-300)
Power BI Service administration — deployment pipelines, workspace governance, gateway configuration, and capacity/refresh management.
Domain fit — healthcare, Pharma/OTC, agency, or marketing-analytics experience; familiarity with CRM/ERP data such as Salesforce and NetSuite.

Tech Stack

Business Intelligence: Power BI (Desktop & Service), DAX, Power Query (M)

Collaboration & Dev Tools: GitHub, Jira, Microsoft Teams

Growth in trusted self-service reporting.

title: Senior Analyst, Assortment
description:
The Senior Assortment Analyst owns the analytical framework behind assortment planning, productivity measurement, and new item performance. This role sets the SKU-level methodology the business plans against and delivers the recommendations that shape what we carry, how deep we buy, and when we exit.

Working within the Merchandise Planning & Analytics organization, the Senior Analyst designs and owns assortment productivity reporting, leads rationalization analysis end to end, and owns the analytical model behind new product introduction forecasting and post-launch scorecarding. The role also sets analytical standards for the team and provides technical guidance to less experienced analysts.

This is a senior individual contributor role with direct influence over assortment decisions, regular exposure to Merchant and Planning leadership, and a clear path toward Manager-level roles in merchandise planning or analytics.

Key Responsibilities

Assortment Analytics


Own assortment productivity reporting: design, own, and continuously improve SKU and category-level reporting covering velocity, sell-through, margin contribution, and inventory productivity; establish the definitions and data lineage the organization plans against
Lead rationalization analysis: own the analytical case for tail SKU exit, consolidation, and transition; quantify the sales, margin, and productivity impact and present recommendations directly to Merchant and Planning leadership
Own depth and breadth methodology: build and maintain the models that determine how deeply the business invests in individual items and programs, including price point coverage and good-better-best architecture
Size the whitespace opportunity: lead market, consumer, and competitive analysis that identifies assortment gaps, quantifies the opportunity, and informs line review strategy
Set analytical standards: define the methodology, assumptions, and QA standards used across assortment analytics, and review the work of junior analysts for accuracy and rigor


New Item & Program Performance


Own launch scorecards: build and own pre- and post-launch performance scorecards; diagnose forecast variance and translate the findings into forward-looking assumptions
Own transition analytics: lead item transition and end-of-life analysis to ensure clean exits, protected margin, and minimal residual inventory exposure
Improve forecast accuracy: partner with Demand Planning to refine new item forecast methodology using post-launch performance and read-and-react learning


Reporting & Partnership


Deliver executive-ready analytics: produce assortment reporting on an established cadence and translate it into a clear point of view for senior leadership, not just a set of numbers
Advise Merchants and Planners: act as the analytical partner of record for assigned categories, shaping the question as often as answering it and challenging assumptions where the data warrants
Lead complex ad hoc analysis: scope, structure, and deliver the ambiguous, high-stakes analysis behind in-season decisions and line review preparation
Build scalable tooling: automate recurring analysis and move the team toward self-service reporting so analytical capacity shifts from production to interpretation


Success Metrics

In the first 12 months, the Senior Analyst, Assortment Planning will be evaluated on:


Analytical Ownership: Assortment productivity reporting owned end to end, delivered accurately and on cadence, and adopted as the standing input to line reviews
Rationalization Impact: Rationalization analysis led through at least one full cycle, with quantified and realized productivity improvement
Influence: Recognized by Merchant and Planning leadership as a trusted advisor whose analysis changes decisions
Capability Building: Demonstrable improvement in the automation and consistency of assortment reporting, and evidence of developing junior analysts

title: Customer Success Performance Insight Analyst
description:
Who We Are

At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.

We’re helping businesses get off the ground by enabling them to focus on running their business. We solve HR issues. We’re data-driven and never stop iterating. Our Values

If this sounds like you, you’ll fit right in.

Who You Are

You are a data-driven operator who thinks like a builder and brings rigorous systems thinking to Customer Experience (CX) analytics. You see fragmented CX processes as opportunities to build scalable, durable data infrastructure. You thrive at the intersection of CX, data analysis, and operations - turning complex datasets, customer interactions, and performance signals into clear, actionable insights that drive business outcomes.

You bring a combination of analytical rigor, systems architecture, and customer operations expertise. You're comfortable working with large datasets across multiple platforms, writing advanced, performant SQL every day to query and model that data, designing performant dashboards and reporting frameworks, and identifying patterns and root causes across customer journeys. You don't just report on data - you build systems that enable teams to access and act on insights independently. You approach every operational problem with a bias toward automation and systems that scale.

You have genuine depth in modern analytics platforms and understand how data flows through customer-facing and internal systems. You're forward-thinking about AI and automation, but apply critical judgment about what requires human expertise and what can be intelligently automated. You bring structure and follow-through to data governance, process design, and knowledge systems so that insights compound over time.

You are highly detail-oriented and structured, with a strong sense of ownership over the systems and analytics foundations you build. At the same time, you are a collaborative partner who can work cross-functionally with stakeholders across Customer Success, Support, Product, Engineering, and Data & Analytics to translate business questions into data strategy, ensure data quality, and operationalize insights at scale.

Design and build scalable reporting frameworks and data pipelines that enable self-service insights across CSO and cross-functional teams
Own data strategy and architecture for CX operations - defining metrics, data models, and governance standards that support both operational reporting and strategic analysis
Architect dashboards and data exports that provide visibility into customer health, agent performance, and operational efficiency across multiple systems (Rippit, knowledge platforms, support tools, etc.)
Build systems thinking around CX data - distinguish between process issues and structural problems, knowing when to optimize existing flows vs. redesign systems
Analytics & Insights
Analyze large, complex datasets to identify behavioral patterns, performance drivers, and root causes that inform opportunities to improve workflows, eliminate inefficiencies, and scale operations
Use conversation analytics, transactional data, and customer interaction data to create reports on revenue-impacting and experience-driving topics
Conduct deep-dive analysis on CSO performance, customer satisfaction trends, and operational health metrics; translate findings into clear recommendations
Define, instrument, and track KPIs related to customer experience, agent performance, operational efficiency, and AI accuracy
Partner with leadership to influence strategy using data-driven storytelling and evidence-based insights
AI & Automation
Design, train, and implement LLM prompts to scale QA automation, insight generation, and customer feedback synthesis
Evaluate AI-generated outputs (chatbots, automated QA, etc.) for accuracy, clarity, and business impact; build feedback loops to continuously improve AI systems
Identify opportunities for automation in QA processes, reporting, and customer feedback analysis; design workflows that leverage AI to free CSO teams for higher-leverage work
Continuously ask: what work here requires human judgment, and what can be intelligently automated? Then build systems to make the right call
Operational Excellence
Own day-to-day operational maintenance and optimization of analytics platforms (Rippit, dashboards, metrics, reporting pipelines, data exports)
Act as primary liaison with analytics platform providers to troubleshoot issues, identify opportunities for optimization, and maintain system reliability
Ensure data integrity and governance across CX systems and reporting layers; establish standards for data quality, documentation, and access
Build and maintain knowledge systems (dashboards, runbooks, documentation) structured for both human and AI consumption
Manage NPS outreach (including direct customer follow-up) and conduct targeted deep dives to be presented to Leadership; synthesize findings into operational insights
Cross-Functional Partnerships
Collaborate closely with Research and Voice of Customer (VoC) teams to synthesize insights, translate findings into CSO-specific performance drivers, and identify Customer Experience improvement opportunities
Partner with Support, Enablement, RevOps, Engineering, and Data & Analytics teams to align analytics tooling, data definitions, and insights
Deliver recurring reporting and insights to CSO leadership in digestible formats (dashboards, newsletters, executive summaries)
Translate CSO needs into data requirements and work with Data & Analytics team to build necessary infrastructure
How You Will Do Your Work

As a CS Performance Insights Analyst, how results are achieved is paramount for your success and ultimately results in our success as an organization. In this role, your foundational knowledge, skills, abilities, and personal attributes are anchored in the following competencies:

Systems Thinking - You see operational problems holistically. You can distinguish between process issues and structural problems. You understand how data flows through systems and how changes cascade. You build solutions that compound in value over time.
Consultative - You take an approach that focuses on building relationships with others, understanding their problems, and developing solutions to their challenges through open-ended questions and active listening.
Taking Responsibility - You are accountable, committed, and accepting of ownership for your decisions, actions, and behavior. You ship systems that work and own their outcomes.
Adaptability - You have the ability to adjust your approach or actions in response to changes in your external environment, evolving customer needs, or new data insights.
Solution-Oriented - You identify the source of a question or challenge and provide the right, or a better, way of doing things. You bias toward elegant, scalable solutions over quick fixes.
Curious - You have an innate desire to learn, grow, and understand. You stay current on analytics tools, AI capabilities, and best practices. You ask good questions.
Data Fluency & Rigor - You approach analytical problems with the same rigor as a data analyst. You write advanced SQL fluently, and you understand data quality, statistical thinking, metric definition, and bias. You know how to verify your own work.

In addition, all Justworkers focus on aligning their behaviors to our core values known as COGIS:

Camaraderie - Day to day you can be seen working together toward a higher purpose. You like to have fun. You're an active listener, treat people respectfully, and have a strong desire to know and help others.
Openness - Your default is to be open. You're willing to share information, understand other perspectives, and consider new possibilities. You're curious, ask open questions, and are receptive to thoughts and feedback from others.
Grit - You demonstrate grit by having the courage to commit and persevere. You're committed, earnest, and dive in to get the job done well with a positive attitude.
Integrity - Simply put, do what you say and say what you'll do. You're honest and forthright, have a strong moral compass, and strive to match your words with your actions while leading by example.
Simplicity - Be like Einstein: "Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler."

Advanced SQL proficiency (non-negotiable): you write complex, performant SQL every day - to explore and validate data, build and maintain data models, and power dashboards and reporting. This is a core, daily requirement of the role.
3-5+ years of experience in data analytics, customer analytics, CX operations, quality assurance, or related roles with strong focus on building data systems and frameworks (not just reporting on data)
Demonstrated systems thinking applied to operations - you've designed processes, data flows, or analytics infrastructure that scale beyond manual work
Advanced experience designing and maintaining dashboards, reports, and data pipelines, underpinned by strong hands-on SQL

description:

As part of Veeva, the Crossix team offers the agility of a high-growth team with the stability of a global leader.

The Role

We are hiring recent university graduates to grow the next generation of data analysts through our Analytics Development Program.

The Marketing Data Analyst (MDA) is a member of the internal analytics team focused on product analytics. This team’s primary function is to produce the analytical reports that are incorporated into Veeva Crossix products and shared with customers.

What this role is (and isn’t):


What it IS: A data analytics role. You will be part of our internal analytics team, focusing on backend report generation, quality control, and pressure-testing results. Using SQL, Excel, and our proprietary coding language, you will link marketing data to health data, transforming large datasets into core analytical reports embedded in Veeva Crossix products. Your work will be used to generate the insights our customers use to make business decisions.
What it IS NOT: This is not a client-facing consulting role. If you want to spend your days in external client meetings, presenting slide decks, and advising on marketing strategies, check out the Client Services Associate track. This is also not a software engineering role - your focus is on data logic, manipulation, and insights, not building software architecture.


This role is part of Generation Veeva, and as such you can expect:


A “learn by doing” environment with challenging and impactful work, where you will be expected to learn quickly and deliver early
A collaborative work environment where you will work closely with many levels of our team, from other early-career professionals through senior leaders
Mentorship and continuous professional development opportunities, aiding in your immediate and long-term success at Veeva


The anticipated start date is July 2027.

The Analytics Development Program offers two distinct paths. Please review our other track, the Client Services Associate role, to choose the best fit for your skills and interests.

We welcome you to apply to all roles that align with your skills and interests. See all open opportunities here: Generation Veeva Careers

What You'll Do


Produce Analytics Reports: Own the end-to-end execution, rigorous quality control, and timely delivery of high-value, recurring analytical reports across a large portfolio.
Link Complex Datasets: Connect marketing exposure data to massive, transactional healthcare datasets. Your data manipulation will provide the analytical foundation that helps pharmaceutical and life sciences companies optimize their marketing efforts and ultimately improve patient outcomes.
Formulate Analytical Hypotheses: Transform complex client questions into hypotheses that are testable using SQL, Excel, and Crossix’s proprietary analytical coding language.
Partner Internally with Client Services: Communicate the technical results and methodology of marketing campaign analyses to our Client Services teams, acting as the subject-matter expert on the underlying data logic.
Master Modern Data Tools: Leverage a robust toolkit including SQL, advanced Excel, data visualization suites, and internal platforms to clean, manipulate, and present data effectively.


REQUIREMENTS | We are looking for graduates who meet the following requirements:


Technical Foundation: Intermediate proficiency in SQL, Python, or a comparable coding language. You have a natural comfort with data structures and a knack for logical, step-by-step problem-solving.
High Drive & Performance: A self-starter with a track record of excellence who thrives in a demanding and dynamic environment, and is hungry for rapid professional growth.
Meticulous Attention to Detail: Exceptional precision and a commitment to rigorous quality control. You take pride in catching small errors before they impact the final product.
Effective Communication Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively share technical insights and methodology with our internal client services teams.
Academic Excellence: Bachelor’s degree (any major) with a 3.0 – 4.0 GPA, demonstrating the intellectual curiosity, time management, and work ethic necessary for a high-performance analytics career.
